Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business
hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make
inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the
Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours
prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however,
to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a
presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council must
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits
the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific
agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City
Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  May 11, 2010

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Humphrey.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Perkins, Mayor Pro Tem Rea,
  Mayor Humphrey

ABSENT:  Councilmember Goodhart

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Hogin, Assistant City
  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, Administrative Analyst Davis,
  Minutes Secretary Monson

MAYOR’S REPORT – none

CONSENT AGENDA

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea, seconded by Councilmember Perkins and unanimously
approved that the following Consent Agenda items be approved:

•  MINUTES OF CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF APRIL 27, 2010

•  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT – APRIL 2010

•  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT – APRIL 2010

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC - none

NEW BUSINESS

REQUEST FOR RATE ADJUSTMENT IN REFUSE COLLECTION BY ATHENS
SERVICES

Public Works Director Rigg reported the current agreement with Athens Services allows Athens to
approach the City on an annual basis to request a rate adjustment. The adjustment is based on a
specific formula governed by the change in the CPI and the changes in solid/green waste landfill
CITY COUNCIL
May 11, 2010  1
 disposal costs. Residents are currently charged $31.01 per month for rear-yard services. Applying the
formula would result in an increase of over 13% which exceeds the annual 7% increase allowed in the
agreement. Therefore, the increase is limited to $2.17 per the agreement which results in a new
monthly cost to residents of $33.18. The adjustment would be effective July 1, 2010.

Athens Services has also requested rate adjustments to rates for the use of the 3 Yard, Low Boy and 30
Yard dumpsters whose rates have not changed since 2005. These rate adjustments would be effective
July 1, 2010.

Director Rigg noted that the City is tracking AB32 which may affect solid waste and recycling services
for multi-family dwellings and businesses.

Mayor Humphrey requested that an explanation of the rate increase be included on the next billing
invoice.

Director of Governmental Affairs for Athens Services Chris Carlos indicated that Athens is pleased to
offer innovative ways to enhance refuse collection in PVE. One component is the Material Recovery
Facility which helps Athens to meet and exceed AB939 requirements. He extended an invitation to the
Council to tour the facility.

It was moved by Councilmember Bird, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and unanimously approved
to approve the $2.17 monthly rate increase, per single family residence, to the solid waste and
recycling collection service to be effective July 1, 2010, to bring the total new monthly rate to $33.18.
It is also recommended that Council approve the increase in bin and dumpster rates to be effective July
1, 2010. Staff further recommends that Council approve invoicing for the increase during Athens’ next
available 2010 billing cycle with an explanation of the increase to be included in the invoicing.

Roll Call Vote:

AYES: Councilmember Bird, Councilmember Perkins, Mayor Pro Tem Rea, Mayor Humphrey

NOES: None

ABSENT: Councilmember Goodhart

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report - none

DEMANDS

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and seconded by Councilmember Bird that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council, totaling $207,766.37 be allowed and it was
unanimously approved (Goodhart absent).

CITY COUNCIL
May 11, 2010  2
 It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and seconded by Councilmember Bird that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council No 516948V, 517430V, 517437H to 517438H, 5174439
to 517504 totaling $82,501.35 be allowed and it was unanimously approved (Goodhart absent).

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS

Mayor Pro Tem Rea reported that the CJPIA would like PVE to submit a list of the names of all of the
registered Disaster Workers.

Mayor Humphrey reported her attendance at the Medal of Valor luncheon with Chief Dreiling.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea noted that PVE’s canine team won the recent canine competition in Redondo
Beach. Chief Dreiling confirmed that Officer Joe Hall and Grim did win first place in all categories
and this would be their last competition as Officer Hall is retiring in July.

Council set Tuesday, June 22nd at 5:00 p.m. for the interviews of applicants to the City
Commission/Committees.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business before Council the meeting was adjourned at 8:00 p.m. to Tuesday,
May 25th at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall.

  RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED,

  MICHÉLE D. MONSON, MINUTES SECRETARY

APPROVED:

ROSEMARY HUMPHREY, MAYOR
